subject: Audit log access CSV and retention Qs — Acme pilot follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acme-corp.com>, Tom Reyes <tom@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: audit logs & retention for Acme pilot

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and a few concrete asks so we can get you the evidence Acme needs for the pilot security review.

Key points from call:
- Redwood will surface per-request audit logs (who/what/when) for model inference and data exports.
- Default audit retention is configurable; we discussed 90 vs 365 days and an on-demand export option.
- Exports can be delivered as CSV or NDJSON to an S3 bucket or via a secure transfer link.

Immediate asks from Acme security (per call):
1) Sample export showing columns and anonymization options (CSV preferred).
2) Confirmation that audit records include: timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), actor identity (email or internal user id), action type (model.generate, export.download, key.rotate), resource id (request id / object id), session id, and IP address.
3) Evidence checklist for SOC2-style intake (who to contact and expected turnaround).

I’ve attached a small sample CSV that mirrors the format we typically provide and a short SOC2 intake checklist for reference.

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Marissa (me): deliver initial sample and draft mapping by EOD Monday.
- Dev Patel (cc): confirm exact column names and whether we can include both email and user_id or only pseudonymized ids for exports.
- Jordan Blake (cc): coordinate logistics for S3 bucket or secure share.

Would you like us to stage an export for the pilot date range (2025-12-01 -> 2026-01-09) and deliver to an Acme S3 path, or would you prefer a downloadable link first for review?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A couple clarifying Qs before we ask Procurement to accept an S3 delivery:

1) Column mapping: can you provide the exact column names you’ll export? We need to map them into our SIEM. Specifically we need to know whether you include a clear email address column, or if you only export an internal user_id. If both are available, we need to understand pseudonymization options (HMAC, tokenized id).

2) Retention policy: Acme’s baseline is 90 days for PII-containing logs. Can Redwood support a 90-day retention window for the pilot, and can you provide a signed statement of retention controls? We will want to store the export outside of Redwood; please confirm whether exports include truncated or redacted PII by default.

3) On-demand exports: we need exports in CSV and NDJSON. Is Parquet supported for bulk analytic loads? Also we need each export to include a manifest file with MD5/SHA256 checksums.

4) Access evidence: for our audit records we’ll need an access report that shows exactly who accessed or exported logs and when (user, email, action, timestamp, IP). Can you produce that for an arbitrary date range? We specifically want an export filtered by 2025-12-01 to 2026-01-09 for initial validation.

Attached is our SOC2 evidence questionnaire — key fields are highlighted. Can you also indicate an estimated turnaround for the requested export and any redaction steps you will take?

Appreciate it — if easier we can do a short 20-min runbook review with Dev and your infra engineer.

Thanks,
Lydia Park

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks — quick technical summary and what we can deliver without code changes: 

1) Export formats: we support CSV, NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), and Parquet. We will include a manifest JSON file with SHA256 checksums per object by default.

2) Columns included:
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- request_id
- actor_email (if available)
- actor_user_id (internal id)
- action (model.generate, export.download, key.rotate)
- resource_id
- session_id
- src_ip
- response_status
- bytes_transferred

We can HMAC actor_email on export if Acme prefers not to receive raw emails; HMAC salt is tenant-specific and we can optionally provide a mapping under NDA.

3) Retention: default tenant-level retention is 365 days. We can create a 90-day retention policy for Acme for the pilot window; this is a config change (no code change) and we can backfill exports for 2025-12-01 -> 2026-01-09 on request.

4) Access evidence: our audit pipeline records every administrative export and console access event. We can produce an "access report" with the fields: actor_email, action, timestamp_utc, target_object_id, ip_address, and request_id. We can filter by date range and deliver in CSV or NDJSON.

5) Delivery options: S3 (we will write to Acme-provided bucket with server-side encryption AES256), or provide a pre-signed HTTPS bundle for download from our staging store. Both include manifest and SHA256 sums.

6) Turnaround: once Jordan confirms destination, we can stage and deliver the filtered export plus access report within 48 business hours. If Acme needs mapping from hashed id -> email, that requires NDA + secure channel.

I’ve attached a small sample export (redwood_audit_sample_20260112.csv) and the SOC2 checklist responses draft.

Let me know if you want me to stand up a 20-min runbook call and I’ll include the infra engineer.

—Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai
